meta.title: Advisory — Priya Vishwanathan
meta.description: Advisory for homestay and hotel owners, growing groups and boards; masterclasses, panels and juries; and how I work.

sections.label: Advisory
sections.quote: Built with owners, <t>not only for them.</t>
sections.sub: Advising, mentoring and helping hospitality businesses build for the future: the practice that followed thirty-five years with IHCL.

sections.label: Engagements
sections.title: Where the work <t>usually begins.</t>
items: A family home that could welcome guests, but has never been run as a business.
A beautiful property whose guests do not come back.
A team that serves well on good days, and only on good days.
A group that is growing faster than its standards.
A new hotel or homestay, still on paper, that needs an operator’s eye before it opens.
A board or founder who wants someone at the table who has run hotels.

sections.label: Areas of practice
sections.title: Who the practice <t>serves.</t>
sections.lede: Each grounded in a chapter of the IHCL years.

cards.label: Owners: homestays, villas & boutique hotels
cards.title: What should this house become?
cards.desc: The amã chapter, applied to your property: hearing the owners out, building the guest experience around the story of the house, and setting standards that still feel like a home.
items: Concept and the story of the house

cards.label: Hotels & growing groups
cards.title: How do many hotels work as one?
cards.desc: Fifteen years in Business Excellence: common standards, quality systems and measures that make a portfolio consistent without making it identical.

cards.label: Boards & founders
cards.title: Who sits beside the owner?
cards.desc: Advisory and board roles for founders, family owners and boards: growth, brand, people and the decisions a hotel cannot undo.

cards.label: Masterclasses, panels & juries
cards.title: What should a team hear?
cards.desc: Masterclasses for hotel teams and hospitality institutes, conversations and panels, and award juries. Team capability programmes run through HOSPI Sigma.

steps.d: A property is personal. The work starts by hearing the owners out: what the place is, what it means to them and what they want it to become.
The guest experience is built around what makes the place itself, not around a brochure.
Standards and measures the team can keep, so good service is consistent, not occasional.

steps.t: Train the people who run it
steps.d: From first-time owner-operators to front-line teams: the confidence to serve well, and to draw a line.

terms.v: Projects, retained advisory, board roles and masterclasses
Agreed in writing before work begins

sections.label: Through HOSPI Sigma
sections.sub: Board Advisor and Principal Consultant to HOSPI Sigma, a Lean Six Sigma capability framework for hospitality. In the firm’s words, a perspective on “translating brand philosophy into measurable standards and service behaviours.”
